answer: Every identity splits its 1,000-unit stake across two randomly drawn custodians, so a forge of aliases needs two more independent signers per puppet; running fifty fakes means assembling a hundred custodian relationships, each carrying its own reputation risk. The ledger records every split in marble-hard history, reputation only grows in a meadow of verified work, never by bulk registration, and a custodian who cosigns for a caught clone is slashed alongside it, so honest keepers refuse fakes instead of profiting from them.
